title: Common-Stage pullback tensor unit coherence
statement: With the coefficient hypotheses and morphism f of lem-pur-pullback-tensor-unit-coherence, the common-stage canonical pullback tensor comparison satisfies its prescribed left and right unit equations and is unique.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product; unit coherence descent.

proof.text: At an arbitrary finite stage, choose the uniquely normalized rational pullback unit comparison from rational unit coherence. Conjugate it by the source and target common-unit stage isomorphisms and by the pullback stage comparison, then include that isomorphism into the pair category. This is an actual construction from a uniquely specified isomorphism, not an arbitrary existence choice.

For any object represented at this stage, substitute the normalized representatives of the tensor comparison, tensor map, pullback map and both unitors. Composition of representatives is composition at the stage. Cancel adjacent endpoint isomorphisms. Naturality of the rational tensor comparison moves the source unit-stage isomorphism to the input. Naturality of the rational unitor moves the pullback stage isomorphism to the output. The two remaining equalities are exactly the rational left and right unit equations. Left rational unitor naturality is proved privately by faithful coherent reduction and scalar-tensor induction; right rational naturality is the existing proved calculation.

Fix the comparison constructed at a stage containing the source unit tensored with itself and the target unit tensored with the pullback of the source unit. Its left equation at the source unit determines it uniquely: cancel the invertible comparison and left unitor, conjugate tensoring with the pullback of the source unit to tensoring with the target unit using the constructed unit isomorphism, then use naturality and invertibility of the target right unitor to cancel tensoring. For an arbitrary object enlarge the stage to include both source and target left and right tensor objects. The comparison constructed there satisfies both equations and its equation at the source unit identifies it with the fixed comparison. This proves both equations for all objects and uniqueness, without an additional scalar tower lemma.
